name: Youth Club Leadership and Coaching — Entry Point

stations.why: The shared opener: the floor walked, the emergency plan read and the warm-up done in order before anyone runs.
Feedback that makes a young player want the next rep.
Two teammates in conflict, handled with accountability rather than favour.
A loss reviewed with the players in a way that keeps them in the gym next week.
A young person who says they are struggling, heard and referred on, not handled alone.
The club's older members returning as mentors, with the same safeguards as the coaches.
Mediating between two families, hearing each side before any decision.
The programme ends where the leadership does, with the role handed to someone who can do it.

summary: The entry point for a youth club's coaches and mentors: a session started with the floor checked and the warm-up done, feedback that grows a young player, a teammate conflict handled with accountability, and a mentor who hands the role on. It shares its court stations with the basketball programme, so a club that runs both trains the same coach.
union: AFSCME and SEIU parks-and-recreation staff who run youth programmes; taught against the youth-sport and child-safety guidelines, not a union apprenticeship
